messages.subject: [statnet_help] Using rergm
messages.body_plain:
Hi Avra.  Have you tried using the 'simulate' command in place of  
'rergm'?  The former is part of statnet and basically has replaced  
the latter.  There is an 'nsim'  argument to simulate that controls  
the number of networks simulated.  Thus, you might try the following  
code (without having to load latentnet):

graph = ergm(bank~edges+m2star+mutual+triangles+absdiff("hay")+istar 
(2)+ostar(2))
simnets = simulate(graph, nsim=10)

Hope this helps!

Dave

messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] a problem with read.paj() from network package
messages.body_plain:
Dear List,

I have tried to read a network in pajek format (.net) using the  
read.paj() function of the network package...

the net file should be well formatted, because Pajek and Ucinet read  
it correctly.. but when I try with R, the problem is that it doesn't  
count the right number of nodes: there are 59 nodes in the network  
(Pajek and Ucinet do see this), but read.paj() says there are only 57.

this is the simple sintax I have used:

mynet<-read.paj("net/mynetwork.net")

and here you can find my net file:

http://www.digitaldust.it/dottorato/mmorpg/marzo2004.net

is it a bug?

do I miss something?

thank you,
Simone

messages.subject: [statnet_help] a problem with read.paj() from network package
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] a problem with read.paj() from network package
messages.body_plain:
Hi Simone.

This looks like a bug in read.paj.  By my reading, the code appears  
to be written so that if the largest numbered vertex has no arcs (in  
your example neither 58 nor 59 has any arcs), this problem occurs.   
You'll notice that none of the vertex names was loaded in either,  
which is a symptom of the same problem.

Here is a totally inelegant solution, but it should work for you:   
First, add the line "1 59 1" just after the "*Arcs" line in your  
mynetwork.net file to create an extra arc involving vertex #59.  Then  
type

mynet <- read.paj("net/mynetwork.net") ; mynet[1,59] <- 0

This will correctly read in all 59 nodes, then erase the extra arc  
you created with "1 59 1".    Save your mynet object as an R object,  
then don't forget to delete the extra line in your mynetwork.net file  
when you're finished.

Dave

messages.subject: [statnet_help] New ergm package available for testing
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] New ergm package available for testing
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone.  The statnet team is excited about finally (almost)  
rolling out a new version of the core R package to fit, simulate and  
analyze exponential-family models for networks.

The new package, called ergm, includes all of the old statnet  
functionality plus more stable code, better documentation, additional  
model terms, better control of MCMC constraints, and more.

The statnet package is not going away -- but it will essentially just  
load "ergm" along with other packages.  Thus, statnet will become the  
name for a whole suite of packages, whereas ergm will assume  
statnet's old role as the specific package that does the ERGM  
(exponential-family random graph model) work.

We have just begun the sometimes-complicated process of submitting  
ergm to CRAN (the CRAN entry will include the source code), and  
probably it will be posted within a couple weeks.  We hope to delay  
the CRAN release for just a few days in order to garner some feedback  
from you -- see below.  For now, you can access and test the new ergm  
by typing, in R,
   install.packages("ergm",contrib="http://csde.washington.edu/statnet")
After installation, type library(ergm) to load the software.

The current version is version 1.99, and when the CRAN release goes  
up it will be version 2.0.  We have been testing this new version,  
but naturally there will be some problems that have escaped our  
notice in a package this complex.  For those of you who currently use  
and appreciate statnet, we'd be grateful if you showed us how much  
you enjoy it by beta-testing the new version of ergm and sending us  
any bugs you find in the next week or so.  :)

Thanks in advance!

Dave Hunter
